}}'''Karl Joseph Niklas''' (born 1948) is an American botanist and paleobotanist. He is a [[Liberty Hyde Bailey]] [[Professor Emeritus|Professor]] of [[Professor Emeritus|Plant Biology Emeritus]] in the School of Integrative Plant Science at [[Cornell University]], where he was a member of the faculty from 1978. His research applies physics, engineering and mathematics to plant form, function, and evolution, with particular attention to plant [[biomechanics]] and [[allometry]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Nine faculty members elected AAAS fellows {{!}} Cornell Chronicle |url=https://news.cornell.edu/stories/2018/11/nine-faculty-members-elected-aaas-fellows |access-date=2026-09-28 |website=news.cornell.edu |language=en}}</ref> He is also known for quantitative studies of the plant fossil record.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-08-10 |title=Karl J. Niklas {{!}} American Academy of Arts and Sciences |url=https://www.amacad.org/person/karl-j-niklas |access-date=2026-09-28 |website=www.amacad.org |language=en}}</ref>

== Education ==
Niklas earned his bachelor's degree at [[City College of New York]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Curriculum Vitae |url=https://labs.plantbio.cornell.edu/niklas/Curriculum_Vitae_files/niklascv15.pdf |access-date=June 19, 2025}}</ref> He earned his Ph.D. in [[paleobiology]] from the [[University of Illinois]] in [[1974]] and completed his post-doctoral research at [[Birkbeck, University of London|Birkbeck College]] as a [[Fulbright Program|Fulbright-Hays Fellow]].<ref name="templeton">{{cite web|url=http://www.templeton.org/humble_approach_initiative/Purpose_in_Evolution/part8.html|title=Purpose in Evolution: Participants|publisher=John Templeton Foundation|access-date=11 February 2010|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100412155734/http://www.templeton.org/humble_approach_initiative/Purpose_in_Evolution/part8.html|archive-date=12 April 2010}}</ref>

== Career ==
After working as a curator at the [[New York Botanical Garden]], Niklas joined the Cornell University faculty in 1978. He was promoted to full professor in 1985 and appointed Liberty Hyde Bailey Professor in 2000. Niklas served as president of the [[Botanical Society of America]] from 2008 to 2009 and as editor-in-chief of the ''[[American Journal of Botany]]'' from 1995 to 2004.<ref name="templeton" /> He has published over 480 peer-reviewed papers and authored six books on plant biology topics.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Karl Niklas {{!}} CALS |url=https://cals.cornell.edu/people/karl-niklas |access-date=2025-05-21 |website=cals.cornell.edu |language=en}}</ref> He was elected as a fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2015.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2025-04-28 |title=Karl J. Niklas {{!}} American Academy of Arts and Sciences |url=https://www.amacad.org/person/karl-j-niklas |access-date=2025-06-25 |website=www.amacad.org |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=Karl Joseph Niklas |url=https://www.helixcenter.org/participants/karl-joseph-niklas/ |access-date=2025-08-06 |website=The Helix Center |language=en-US}}</ref>
